name: Classic Margherita Pizza
description: Traditional Neapolitan pizza with fresh mozzarella, basil, and San Marzano tomato sauce
steps: Preheat oven to 475°F (245°C) with a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet.
Stretch the dough into a 12-inch round on a floured surface.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce, leaving a 1-inch border.
Tear mozzarella into chunks and distribute evenly over the sauce.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Top with fresh basil leaves and serve immediately.
tips: For the best crust, let the dough come to room temperature 30 minutes before stretching. Don't overload with toppings.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Tender chicken pieces in a rich, creamy tomato-based curry sauce with aromatic spices
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt, turmeric, chili powder, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the marinated chicken until charred. Set aside.
Sauté onions until golden, then add garlic and ginger paste.
Add tomato purée and cook for 10 minutes until oil separates.
Add garam masala, cumin, and coriander. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in cream, stir well, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the grilled chicken pieces and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with naan or rice.
tips: Marinating overnight intensifies the flavor. Use kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) for authentic restaurant taste.

name: Egg Fried Rice
description: Quick wok-fried rice with scrambled eggs, scallions, and soy sauce
steps: Use day-old rice for the best texture. Break up any clumps.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Scramble the eggs quickly, then push to the side.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add rice and toss vigorously for 2-3 minutes.
Drizzle soy sauce along the edge of the wok.
Add scallions and sesame oil, toss once more, and serve.
tips: The key is HIGH heat and a dry wok. Day-old refrigerated rice gives the best wok hei (smoky flavor).

name: Avocado Toast with Poached Eggs
description: Creamy mashed avocado on sourdough toast topped with perfectly poached eggs
steps: Toast the bread until golden and crispy.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar.
Create a vortex and gently drop in the egg. Poach for 3-4 minutes.
Spread mashed avocado on toast.
Top with the poached egg.
Sprinkle with chili flakes and drizzle with olive oil.
tips: Fresh eggs poach better. The vinegar helps the egg white coagulate quickly.

name: Pasta Aglio e Olio
description: Simple Roman pasta with garlic, olive oil, chili flakes, and parsley
steps: Cook spaghetti in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Thinly slice 6-8 garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat.
Add garlic and chili flakes, cook until garlic is golden (not brown!).
Add drained pasta to the pan with 1/2 cup pasta water.
Toss vigorously until the sauce emulsifies and coats the pasta.
Add chopped parsley, toss, and serve with parmesan.
tips: This dish is all about garlic cooked perfectly — golden, not burnt. The pasta water is essential for creating the silky sauce.

name: Chicken Biryani
description: Fragrant layered rice dish with spiced chicken, saffron, and caramelized onions
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and all spices for 2 hours.
Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes, then parboil until 70% cooked. Drain.
Deep-fry thinly sliced onions until golden brown (birista). Reserve.
Cook the marinated chicken in ghee until 80% done.
Layer: chicken on bottom, then rice, then fried onions, saffron milk, mint, cilantro.
Repeat layers. Seal the pot with dough or tight-fitting lid.
Cook on lowest heat (dum) for 25 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, then gently mix layers and serve with raita.
tips: The dum cooking (slow steam) is crucial. Don't open the lid during cooking. Use aged basmati for the best elongation.

name: Tacos al Pastor
description: Marinated pork tacos with pineapple, onion, cilantro, and salsa verde
steps: Blend dried chilies, garlic, cumin, oregano, vinegar, and pineapple juice into a marinade.
Marinate thinly sliced pork for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
Grill or pan-sear the pork in batches over high heat until charred.
Grill pineapple slices until caramelized.
Dice the pork and pineapple into small pieces.
Warm corn tortillas on a dry skillet.
Assemble: tortilla, pork, pineapple, diced onion, cilantro, and lime juice.
tips: The key is the char on the pork. If you have a vertical rotisserie, use it for authentic trompo-style cooking.

name: Japanese Miso Soup
description: Traditional dashi-based soup with silken tofu, wakame seaweed, and scallions
steps: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer (never boil miso!).
Rehydrate wakame in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Cut silken tofu into small cubes.
Dissolve miso paste in a ladle of warm broth, then stir into the pot.
Add tofu and wakame. Heat gently for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately, garnished with sliced scallions.
tips: Never boil miso — it destroys the beneficial probiotics and dulls the flavor. Add miso last, off the heat.

name: Greek Salad
description: Fresh Mediterranean salad with tomatoes, cucumber, olives, feta, and oregano
steps: Cut tomatoes into wedges and cucumber into half-moons.
Thinly slice red onion into rings.
Combine vegetables in a large bowl.
Add Kalamata olives.
Crumble feta cheese over the top (don't mix in).
Drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
Season with dried oregano, salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lemon.
tips: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find. Traditional Greek salad has no lettuce — just chunky vegetables and a slab of feta.

name: Beef Stir-Fry with Broccoli
description: Tender beef strips with crisp broccoli in a savory garlic-ginger sauce
steps: Slice beef thinly against the grain. Marinate with soy sauce, cornstarch, and sesame oil.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes. Shock in ice water.
Heat wok until smoking. Sear beef in batches (don't overcrowd). Remove.
Add garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add broccoli, then the sauce (soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, water).
Return beef to the wok. Toss everything together for 1 minute.
Thicken with a cornstarch slurry if needed. Serve over rice.
tips: Slice beef while it's partially frozen for thinner, more tender strips. Velveting (marinating with cornstarch) keeps the beef silky.

name: Spinach and Ricotta Stuffed Shells
description: Jumbo pasta shells filled with creamy ricotta and spinach, baked in marinara
steps: Cook pasta shells until just al dente (they'll finish cooking in the oven).
Sauté spinach with garlic until wilted. Squeeze out excess moisture.
Mix ricotta, spinach, half the mozzarella, parmesan, egg, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread a layer of marinara on the bottom of a baking dish.
Fill each shell with the ricotta mixture and arrange in the dish.
Cover with remaining marinara and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25-30 minutes until bubbly and golden.
tips: Drain the ricotta and squeeze the spinach thoroughly — excess moisture makes the shells soggy.

name: Palak Paneer
description: Creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer cheese in aromatic spices
steps: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes. Ice bath, then blend into a smooth purée.
Pan-fry paneer cubes until golden. Set aside.
Sauté cumin seeds, then add onion, garlic, ginger, and green chili.
Add diced tomato and cook until soft.
Add turmeric and garam masala, cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the spinach purée and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add cream and the fried paneer. Simmer 5 more minutes.
Serve hot with naan or rice.
tips: Blanching and ice-bathing the spinach keeps it vibrant green. Adding a pinch of sugar balances the bitterness.

name: Banana Pancakes
description: Fluffy pancakes made with ripe bananas, served with maple syrup and berries
steps: Mash ripe bananas until smooth.
Whisk eggs, milk, melted butter, and vanilla in a bowl.
In another bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Fold wet ingredients into dry — don't overmix (lumps are okay!).
Fold in the mashed banana.
Cook on a buttered griddle over medium heat. Flip when bubbles form on the surface.
Serve stacked with maple syrup, fresh berries, and a pat of butter.
tips: The riper the banana, the sweeter and more flavorful. Overmixing develops gluten and makes tough pancakes.

name: Tom Yum Soup
description: Hot and sour Thai soup with shrimp, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime
steps: Bring water or stock to a boil. Add lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse the aromatics.
Add mushrooms and tomatoes. Cook 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until pink (2-3 minutes).
Season with fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chili paste.
Stir in coconut milk for a creamy version (tom kha style).
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately.
tips: Don't eat the lemongrass and galangal pieces — they're for flavoring only. Adjust the chili and lime to your taste.

name: Caesar Salad
description: Classic Caesar with romaine, homemade dressing, croutons, and shaved parmesan
steps: Make croutons: cube bread, toss with olive oil and garlic, bake at 400°F until golden.
Make dressing: blend anchovy, garlic, lemon juice, mustard, egg yolk, and olive oil.
Wash and dry romaine, tear into pieces.
Toss romaine with dressing until evenly coated.
Add croutons and toss gently.
Shave parmesan over the top with a vegetable peeler.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.
tips: Use the inner hearts of romaine for the best crunch. The dressing emulsifies better if ingredients are at room temperature.

name: Vegetable Pad Thai
description: Rice noodles stir-fried with tofu, bean sprouts, peanuts, and tamarind sauce
steps: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 20 minutes until pliable. Drain.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and sugar for the sauce.
Press and cube tofu. Pan-fry until golden and crispy.
Scramble eggs in the wok. Push to the side.
Stir-fry garlic, then add noodles and sauce. Toss for 2 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and scallions. Toss for 30 seconds.
Plate with crushed peanuts, lime wedge, and chili flakes.
tips: Don't over-soak the noodles or they'll turn mushy. The wok should be screaming hot for the best results.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, served with crusty bread
steps: Sauté diced onion and bell pepper in olive oil until softened.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and chili flakes. Cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Make wells in the sauce and crack eggs into them.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 5-7 minutes until whites are set but yolks are runny.
Crumble feta cheese over the top.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve in the skillet with crusty bread.
tips: Keep the heat low once you add the eggs — too much heat will overcook the yolks. Serve straight from the pan.

name: Chicken Quesadillas
description: Crispy tortillas filled with seasoned chicken, melted cheese, peppers, and salsa
steps: Season chicken with cumin, chili powder, and salt. Cook until done, then shred.
Sauté bell pepper and onion until slightly charred.
Layer cheese, chicken, and vegetables on half a tortilla. Fold over.
Cook in a skillet with a little oil over medium heat.
Press down gently. Flip when golden and crispy (3-4 minutes per side).
Cut into triangles.
Serve with sour cream, salsa, and guacamole.
tips: Use a mix of cheddar and mozzarella for the best melt. Don't overfill or they'll be hard to flip.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: Creamy Arborio rice with mixed mushrooms, parmesan, and white wine
steps: Heat stock in a saucepan and keep at a gentle simmer.
Sauté mushrooms in butter until golden. Season and set aside.
In the same pan, cook onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes until edges become translucent.
Deglaze with white wine and stir until absorbed.
Add stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, waiting until each is absorbed.
Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Fold in mushrooms, butter, and parmesan. Rest 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Never wash Arborio rice — the starch is what makes risotto creamy. Keep stirring and adding stock gradually.

name: Hummus with Pita
description: Ultra-smooth chickpea dip with tahini, lemon, and garlic, served with warm pita
steps: Drain chickpeas. For ultra-smooth hummus, remove the skins by rubbing between towels.
Blend tahini and lemon juice first for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add chickpeas, garlic, cumin, and salt. Blend for 3-4 minutes.
Stream in ice water while blending until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust lemon, salt, and garlic.
Plate in a shallow bowl, create a swirl, drizzle with olive oil and paprika.
Serve with warm pita bread, vegetables, or falafel.
tips: The secret is blending tahini and lemon FIRST — it creates an ultra-creamy base. Ice water makes it fluffier than olive oil.

name: Korean Bibimbap
description: Mixed rice bowl with seasoned vegetables, beef, fried egg, and gochujang sauce
steps: Cook rice. For dolsot (stone pot) style, cook in a hot stone bowl for crispy bottom.
Marinate beef in soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and sugar. Pan-sear quickly.
Blanch and season each vegetable separately: spinach with sesame oil, carrots with salt, etc.
Fry an egg sunny-side up with crispy edges.
Arrange rice in a bowl. Top with vegetables, beef, and egg in sections.
Add a generous spoonful of gochujang sauce.
Mix everything together thoroughly before eating. Top with sesame seeds.
tips: The beauty is in the presentation — arrange each topping neatly in its own section. Mix vigorously before eating!

name: French Omelette
description: Classic French-style omelette: pale yellow exterior, creamy custardy center
steps: Whisk 3 eggs vigorously with salt until completely homogeneous.
Heat butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat until foaming subsides.
Pour in eggs. Immediately start stirring with a fork while shaking the pan.
When eggs are mostly set but still creamy on top, stop stirring.
Add cheese and chives to one side.
Tilt the pan and fold the omelette onto itself.
Roll out onto a warm plate, seam-side down. Brush with butter for shine.
tips: A perfect French omelette has NO color — pale yellow only. The inside should be baveuse (creamy, like soft curds).

name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Burrito Bowl
description: Roasted sweet potatoes with black beans, corn, avocado, and lime crema
steps: Cube sweet potatoes, toss with cumin, chili powder, paprika, oil, and salt.
Roast at 425°F (220°C) for 25 minutes until caramelized.
Cook rice and season with lime juice and cilantro.
Warm black beans with garlic and cumin.
Make lime crema: mix sour cream, lime juice, and salt.
Assemble bowls: rice, sweet potato, black beans, corn, sliced avocado.
Drizzle with lime crema and garnish with cilantro.
tips: Spread sweet potatoes in a single layer for maximum caramelization. Don't stir them during roasting.

name: Teriyaki Salmon
description: Pan-seared salmon glazed with homemade teriyaki sauce, served with steamed rice
steps: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small saucepan. Simmer until slightly thickened.
Pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper.
Sear salmon skin-side down in a hot oiled pan for 4 minutes.
Flip and cook 2 more minutes.
Pour teriyaki sauce into the pan. Baste the salmon for 1 minute.
Serve over steamed rice.
Garnish with sliced scallions and sesame seeds.
tips: Start skin-side down for crispy skin. Don't move the fish while searing — let the Maillard reaction work.

name: Caprese Salad
description: Simple Italian salad with fresh mozzarella, ripe tomatoes, basil, and balsamic
steps: Slice fresh mozzarella and tomatoes into equal-thickness rounds.
Alternate tomato and mozzarella slices on a platter, overlapping slightly.
Tuck fresh basil leaves between each pair.
Drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
Add a balsamic reduction drizzle.
Season with flaky salt and freshly cracked pepper.
Serve immediately at room temperature.
tips: This dish is only as good as its ingredients. Use the best in-season tomatoes, fresh buffalo mozzarella, and quality olive oil.

name: Dal Tadka
description: Comfort lentil dal with a sizzling tempering of cumin, garlic, and dried chilies
steps: Wash and pressure cook toor dal with turmeric, salt, and water until soft (3-4 whistles).
Mash the dal to a smooth consistency. Adjust water for desired thickness.
For the tadka: heat ghee in a small pan until very hot.
Add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, and dried red chili. Let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, garlic, ginger, and green chili. Sauté 30 seconds.
Add diced onion and tomato. Cook until tomato is soft.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal. Mix and simmer 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and a squeeze of lemon. Serve with rice or roti.
tips: The tadka must sizzle when it hits the dal — that's where the magic happens. Use ghee, not oil, for authentic flavor.

name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
description: The perfect grilled cheese: crispy golden bread with gooey melted cheese
steps: Butter the outside of each bread slice generously.
Spread a thin layer of mustard on the inside.
Layer cheese (use a mix for the best melt).
Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat, covered, for 3-4 minutes per side.
Press down gently with a spatula.
The cheese should be fully melted and the bread deep golden brown.
Cut diagonally and serve immediately.
tips: Low and slow is the secret — medium-low heat lets the cheese melt before the bread burns. Mayo instead of butter makes an even crispier crust.

name: Ramen
description: Rich shoyu ramen with soft-boiled egg, chashu pork, nori, and scallions
steps: Make tare: combine soy sauce, mirin, garlic, and ginger. Simmer 5 minutes.
Simmer pork belly in the tare for 20 minutes. Slice for chashu.
Soft-boil eggs (6 min 30 sec), peel, and marinate in leftover tare.
Heat chicken stock and add 2-3 tablespoons of tare to each bowl.
Cook ramen noodles according to package. Don't overcook!
Place noodles in the broth.
Top with chashu slices, halved marinated egg, corn, nori, mushrooms, and scallions.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve immediately — ramen waits for no one!
tips: The tare (seasoning concentrate) is the soul of ramen. Make extra and store it — it keeps for weeks in the fridge.

name: Overnight Oats
description: No-cook oats soaked overnight with chia seeds, berries, and honey
steps: Combine oats, milk, yogurt, and chia seeds in a jar.
Add honey and vanilla extract. Stir well.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (or at least 6 hours).
In the morning, stir and adjust consistency with more milk if needed.
Top with sliced banana, fresh berries, and a drizzle of honey.
Optional: add nuts, granola, or nut butter for extra texture.
tips: The chia seeds absorb liquid and create a pudding-like texture. Use a 1:1 ratio of oats to liquid for thick oats.

name: Fish Tacos
description: Crispy battered fish in corn tortillas with cabbage slaw and chipotle mayo
steps: Make chipotle mayo: blend mayonnaise, chipotle peppers, lime juice, and garlic.
Make slaw: toss shredded cabbage with lime juice, cilantro, and salt.
Make batter: whisk flour, beer, cumin, and salt until smooth.
Cut fish into strips. Season with salt and cumin.
Dip fish in batter and fry at 375°F until golden and crispy (3-4 minutes).
Warm corn tortillas on a dry skillet.
Assemble: tortilla, slaw, crispy fish, chipotle mayo, and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Use a light, flaky white fish like cod or mahi-mahi. The beer batter should be the consistency of thin pancake batter.
